validity.recommendation: none needed — real, FERC-certificated (CP23-15), correctly classified interstate gas transmission project; caveat is the spec/location corrections filed separately below
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real. TC Energy's own project page (tcenergy.com/operations/natural-gas/WRP/, live, updated through Nov 2025) and project fact sheet describe a specific, dated, multi-year FERC-certificated project (pre-file Feb 2022, FERC application filed Oct 2022, FERC certificate issued Dec 2023, notice-to-proceed Mar 2024, construction Nov 2024-2025, full commercial in-service Nov 1, 2025). Independently, EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects dataset (16 releases, Oct 2022 through Aug 2026, tracked locally in sources/eia_pipeline_projects/) carries this exact project under docket PF22-5 (pre-filing) then CP23-15 (certificated), tracking it from 'Pre-applied' (2022-10) through 'Construction' (2024-04 on) to 'Completed' (2026-01 release, completed_date 2025-11-01). Two independent origins (TC Energy + EIA) confirm the project exists and is complete/operating. CLASSIFICATION: correctly a gas transmission project — EIA's own 'pipeline_type' field for this project reads 'Interstate' (FERC-jurisdictional NGA section 7(c) certificate, docket CP23-15), consistent with GEM's PipelineType=transmission. It is a physical-pipe REPLACEMENT project (TC Energy: 'replacing approximately 51-miles existing pipeline ... with new pipeline'; EIA pre-filing note: 'replacing approx. 48 miles of small diameter p/l with approx 51 miles of larger diameter p/l'), not a compression-only expansion — so the repo's 'expansion with no new physical pipe -> LengthKnown=0' rule does NOT apply here: this project laid ~51 route-miles of new larger-diameter pipe (confirmed physically: PL-1 10.9-11 mi/36-in in McHenry County IL, PL-2 16 mi in Washington/Waukesha Counties WI, PL-3 24 mi in Waupaca/Outagamie/Winnebago Counties WI = ~51 mi total, per TC Energy's own construction-update log), so LengthKnown must carry the real new-pipe mileage rather than 0 or blank. DUPLICATE CHECK (orchestrator cross-row instruction): re-verified, from my own sources, the separation from P2501 (Alberta Xpress Expansion Project, same parent pipeline_name 'ANR Gas Pipeline'). TC Energy maintains WRP and Alberta Xpress as two entirely separate project pages/fact sheets with no overlapping docket, geography, capacity or timeline: WRP is FERC docket CP23-15, Wisconsin/Illinois (Zone 7 pipe replacement + Kewaskum/Weyauwega compressor upgrades), 144,000 Dth/d, in-service Nov 2025; Alberta Xpress is FERC docket CP20-484-000, Michigan->Louisiana (one greenfield compressor station, Evangeline Parish LA, capacity lease with Great Lakes Gas Transmission), 165,000 Dth/d, in-service Jan 2023. These are confirmed-distinct ANR expansion projects, not a relabel/double-count. No merge action needed on either PID.

validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's recorded 48.0 mi / 14,22,30,36-in / 150.00 MMcf/d matches EXACTLY the EIA 'Pre-applied' record tracked under docket PF22-5 (releases Oct2022 through Jan2024, e.g. EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjects_Jan2024.xlsx sheet 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects' row 122: 48 mi, diameter '14, 22, 30, 36', additional_capacity 150 MMcf/d) — i.e. the sheet reflects the project as originally pre-filed in Feb 2022, before FERC certification. Once FERC issued the certificate (Dec 2023, docket CP23-15), EIA's tracking switched to the certificated scope and has read 51 mi / '30,36' in / 144 MMcf/d in every release from Apr2024 (Construction) through Aug2026 (Completed) without change — e.g. EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjectsAug2026.xlsx sheet 'Historical Projects (1996-2024)' row 1205: miles=51, pipeline_diameter_inches='30,36', additional_capacity_mmcf_d=144, status=Completed, completed_date=2025-11-01. TC Energy's own live project page and fact sheet (both independent of EIA) corroborate the AS-BUILT numbers, not the sheet's pre-file numbers: fact sheet states 'replacing approximately 51-miles ... existing pipeline ... with larger diameter, new pipeline' and 'an incremental 144,000 dekatherms per day of natural gas capacity' (144,000 Dth/d ~ 144 MMcf/d, the same Dth/MMcf convention used elsewhere on this sheet, e.g. P2578); the live page's construction-update log itemizes the built segments as PL-1 (10.9-11 mi, 36-inch, McHenry County IL), PL-2 (16 mi, Washington/Waukesha Counties WI) and PL-3 (24 mi, Waupaca/Outagamie/Winnebago Counties WI), summing to ~51 mi. TC Energy's page independently states the 36-inch diameter for PL-1 specifically ('the replacement of 11 miles of 36-inch pipeline (PL-1) ... has been completed'); it does not itself give a diameter for PL-2/PL-3, so the '30-inch' portion of the diameter set rests on EIA alone (all EIA releases count as one origin) — noted as a partial-corroboration caveat. Two independent origins (TC Energy + EIA, both post-certification/post-completion) agree the built project is 51 mi / 144 MMcf/d, and only the 36-in diameter has full two-origin support; treat length and capacity as high tier, diameter as medium.
